solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A pest's not the first problem for garden plant

indicators.note: the opening letter of the synonym for pest's is dropped

parts.note: a fly is a pest, so pest's gives fly's
a sum is an arithmetic problem set in class

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that some insect is not the worst trouble facing a flowerbed plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' cuts F from FLYS, leaving LYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alyssum is a low-growing flowering plant common in garden borders, an example of the category.

clue.text: American artist and writer wants a coffee

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, something to write with

explanation.surface: An American painter and an author both want a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabica is the most widely grown species of coffee bean.

clue.text: Son missing risky horse sports? Riding was part of it

indicators.note: the letter for son is left out of the pool of letters
the letters sport about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Horse riding seems a natural part of risky equestrian sports, son excepted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ridings were the three historic divisions of this English county (North, East, West); 'Riding' looks like horse riding.
explanation.definitionFit: The county was historically split into three administrative areas called Ridings, so a Riding formed part of it.

clue.text: Hold up a retail outlet

definitions.meaning: to delay or play for time
a booth or stand selling goods at a market

explanation.surface: A robbery at a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to delay something, and a small market booth from which goods are sold.

clue.text: State of Maine's not changing

indicators.note: the letters keep changing places to form another word

explanation.surface: An observation that the state of Maine never alters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of Maine' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'State'.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty US states, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: The best conducted Brahms and Liszt

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best of it
led, as an orchestra is led or guided

explanation.surface: A music review: the finest performance conducted works by Brahms and Liszt.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for 'pissed', British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for intoxicated, and pickled is a colloquial synonym for drunk.

clue.text: Turn to bigwig upon whom everything depends

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun, fair because it describes the central person on whom everything turns

indicators.note: turn means turn round, so the following letters are read backwards

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person, a bigwig

explanation.surface: Appealing to the important person who controls everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a definition but reverses TO VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, the central figure in an organisation, the person whose role holds everything together.

clue.text: Chap needs a medicine, being unable to move

parts.note: cat is old slang for a man, as in a cool cat
a tonic is a restorative medicine

explanation.surface: A man laid up and needing medication because he cannot get up.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonia is a state of stupor or rigidity in which a person stays motionless.

clue.text: Most insignificant start for Leyton Orient

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: A sports report on a minor debut for Leyton Orient, a London football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is an East London football club, so the surface reads as one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, meaning smallest in importance.

clue.text: Sound as a bell after long eating in moderation

indicators.note: the bell sound comes after the word for long

parts.note: to die for something is to long for it, as in dying for a drink
ting is the light ringing sound of a bell

explanation.surface: Someone fit and healthy after long eating sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy but is a ringing noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieting means restricting one's food intake, which is eating sparingly.

clue.text: Regularly aboard that vessel

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the following words at a steady interval

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sailor pointing out someone often seen on a particular ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery from the heart, and arteries are blood vessels.

clue.text: New member's no pervert

parts.note: to vitiate is to corrupt or debase, a verb sense of pervert

explanation.surface: Reassurance that the latest recruit to a club is not a deviant.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice in a religious order or other body is a newly admitted member on probation.

clue.text: Victor breaks brassy bust

indicators.note: the letter for Victor breaks into the middle of the other word

parts.note: brassy means cheeky or impudent
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Victor smashes a brass statue bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpture but means bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bust means being unable to pay one's debts, the plain meaning of bankrupt.

clue.text: Three times I carry uniform for all the players

indicators.note: the group of letters carries the next letter within it

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, written three times over
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A soldier boasts of carrying the kit for the whole team three times over.
explanation.definitionFit: In a musical score tutti marks a passage played by the whole ensemble together.

clue.text: Article by young woman is unsuitable

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a girl is judged inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is out of place or wrong, hence inappropriate for the occasion.

clue.text: Resistance force in south of France is caught unawares

indicators.note: the letters go in the French word

parts.note: sud is French for south
R is the physics symbol for resistance
to prise is to force open with leverage

explanation.surface: Wartime: French Resistance fighters in southern France ambush someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' suggests the wartime French underground but gives just R.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surprised is to be taken off guard, the same as being caught unprepared.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory conclusion is displeasing

parts.note: off means not up to standard, as in an off day
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a disappointing finale spoils the whole story.
explanation.definitionFit: Offending as an adjective means causing annoyance or upset, much as unpleasant things do.

clue.text: Nun flew off, having picked up live spider

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters go astray
in a down entry, picked up means raised, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A nun fled in fright after catching a live spider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges NUN FLEW into FUNNELW; 'picked up' turns BE into EB.
explanation.definitionFit: The funnel-web is a venomous Australian spider, named for its funnel-shaped web.

clue.text: One covers for magazine including summary that's inaccurate

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the outer letters include the summary between them
the covers of a word are its outside letters

parts.note: a précis is a summary

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for a magazine writer with a digest that is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecise means not exact, so it describes something lacking accuracy.

clue.text: Determine beforehand — smart clothes or red pants?

indicators.note: the first word dresses or wraps round the scrambled letters

parts.note: to smart is to sting, and a pain is a sting

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, signalling the letters are a mess

explanation.surface: A fashion question: should one wear elegant clothes or red trousers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' and 'pants' both look like clothing words, but 'smart' means sting and 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, here signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To preordain is to decree or fix an outcome in advance, as fate is said to.

clue.text: Dash out of hospital with a remedy

indicators.note: the hospital letter is taken out of the word for dash

parts.note: panache is flamboyant style or dash

explanation.surface: A patient rushes out of hospital clutching a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a verb of haste but means style.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure-all, a remedy for every ill.

clue.text: Drink some cappucino after knocking it back

indicators.note: knocking back a drink fits the surface, but here the letters are read in the opposite direction
only part of the word is used, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Someone downs part of a coffee, gulping it in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes APPUC from inside the coffee word; 'knocking it back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuppa is British colloquial for a cup of tea, the nation's standard hot beverage.

clue.text: Cruel Cockney said to be naive

indicators.note: the word is spoken in a Cockney accent, which drops the H at the start

parts.note: heartless means cruel

explanation.surface: A Londoner calls someone unkind, though they are merely innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, known for dropping initial H, so 'heartless' comes out without it.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means simple, without guile or sophistication, which is close to unsophisticated.

clue.text: Divorce, swapping partners? Surely not!

indicators.note: in bridge North and South are partners, so one compass letter is exchanged for its partner

parts.note: to sever is to separate or cut apart

explanation.surface: An outraged reaction to news of a couple splitting up after wife-swapping.
explanation.walkthrough: S (South) is replaced by N (North), its partner at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: Both exclamations express disbelief, so the interjection is an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Italian scorer exaggerated, avoiding extremes

indicators.note: the synonym loses its first and last letters

parts.note: overdid means exaggerated or went too far

explanation.surface: An Italian football striker hammed up a dive, but not too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests football but means composer of scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian composer, and a composer writes musical scores.

clue.text: Penny gets in secret supply, being far-sighted

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

indicators.note: read as supple-y, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A penny-pinching person squirrels away a hidden stockpile, planning ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' as an adverb (supplely) rearranges IN SECRET to RESCIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescient person foresees events, which is what far-sightedness in judgement means.

clue.text: Quietly encourage removal of undesirable elements

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to urge is to press or encourage

explanation.surface: A discreet push for getting rid of unwanted people.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is the expulsion of disloyal or unwanted people from an organisation.

clue.text: Could be Coco Chanel on vacation getting personal

indicators.note: the word is vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving its outside letters

parts.note: own means personal, belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: Coco Chanel on holiday, taking some private time.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a famous circus performer in Britain; Coco Chanel the designer is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco is an example: the stage name of a celebrated circus funnyman in Britain.

clue.text: Sailors from Irish port proceed on a twisty course

indicators.note: sailors from the port make that port's crew, so the place name comes first

parts.note: Cork is a port city in the south of Ireland, given here in its possessive form
a crew is a ship's company of sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen from an Irish harbour set off on a winding voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to corkscrew is to move along a spiralling path, twisting as it goes.

clue.text: Somebody should hold power, I suppose

indicators.note: the first word holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: one means a person, as in one should
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A political opinion: someone ought to be in charge, I reckon.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state a view, close in sense to supposing or thinking.

clue.text: Song with finale about woman Theseus abandoned

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for finale is read backwards

parts.note: a finale is the end

explanation.surface: An opera aria with a closing section telling of a woman left by Theseus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she helped Theseus escape the labyrinth and he deserted her on Naxos.

clue.text: Forbidding person's standards?

explanation.surface: A question whether a censorious person's moral standards are at issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standards' looks like moral principles but means flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a military flag, and banners are flags or ensigns, so these are synonyms.
